speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what are the mechanisms for overseeing recycling programmes by state agencies and vendors to ensure that recycling is completed as promised; and (b) whether there will be a review to strengthen the system in light of news reports on issues with implementing such a programme.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how does the Ministry ensure that recyclables collected are properly recycled according to the intended objectives as published; and (b) how many cases of collected recyclables being misused have been reported in the past five years.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment how does the Ministry overcome challenges that may prevent more regular and public reporting on the efficiency and effectiveness of sustainability programmes that it implements through third party vendors.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Under the Extended Producer Responsibility scheme for e-waste, NEA requires the scheme operator to send the collected e-waste for proper treatment at licensed e-waste recycling facilities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They must also submit regular reports to NEA on the amount of e-waste received and processed.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Under the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movement of Hazardous Wastes and Their Disposal, which Singapore is a party to, it is illegal to export hazardous and other wastes as defined by the Basel Convention, without Prior Informed Consent from the state of import or transit.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Relevant permits are also required from NEA under the Hazardous Waste (Control of Export, Import and Transit) Act.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For the export of recyclables that are not covered by the Basel Convention, such as sorted streams of ferrous, non-ferrous metals and textiles, companies would have to adhere to the relevant domestic regulations of the importing countries.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The companies would also have to be accountable to the organisers of the recycling programme and the donors of the recyclables, based on contractual agreements and conditions that were agreed upon.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: All segments of society have a part to play in recycling right to achieve our vision of a zero-waste nation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We need to strike a balance between ensuring appropriate levels of regulation and governance, and not imposing overly onerous requirements which would inadvertently discourage voluntary recycling initiatives.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The Minister mentioned that there will be regular checks conducted on the premises.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can I just ask how regular will these checks be?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And I have two supplementary questions for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: One, can the Government encourage more private sector participation to recycle items like sports shoes, like in this case, so that we can minimise the volume of shoes actually being thrown away and being incinerated or in the case of being disposed of overseas, being dumped in landfills?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Number two, will the Government consider giving more incentives to companies to attract them to take part in such recycling programmes?

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On how regular such checks should be made, I am not going to be able to tell Mr Tan with accuracy as to how much time, how many days or how many weeks and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But you have got to leave some discretion to the project partners and if Mr Tan heard my answer earlier, Yok Impex was actually a subcontractor engaged by one of the partners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is not an entity that SportSG deals with directly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, the degree of regularity should also depend on the extent to which the number of shoes collected and aggregated at the various centres reach a certain level that makes commercial sense for the partners to then go and collect it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, I would say, we leave the precise engineering of the timetable to the partners to deal with, but I would like to assure Mr Tan that one of the learning points from this is precisely to also conduct these checks often and unannounced, so that there will be not just a check itself but also the whole framework and a system, to deter activities that do not comply with the contractual scope of the obligations.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As part of our Zero Waste Nation vision, we would like to encourage all consumers and users to reduce, reuse and recycle.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we do welcome companies or non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to promote to every one of us to do more of reducing, reusing and recycling.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, that is why NEA looks at supporting local capabilities, for example, in recycling.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Grants are provided for facilities to build our capabilities, like in this case, we supported BT Sports, one of the project's partners, in building the facility to convert the sport shoes into granules for use in rubber flooring.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On top of that, we also have funds like the SG Eco Fund that will provide financial resources for both corporate as well as community organisations to promote environmental sustainability and the likes of rubber shoe recycling would certainly be something we would be happy to support.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Corporations and organisations are welcome to apply or talk to NEA and the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) about their interest, and we can see how we can facilitate that.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope this episode would not deter our Sport Singapore from doing such efforts.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that investigations are still ongoing, and this is a question for Minister Edwin Tong.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister mentioned about tweaking, fine-tuning and tightening the process downstream with the subcontractors.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are there any contractual mechanisms that Sport Singapore can impose on its partners to similarly have such monitoring mechanisms or tightening of that process downstream on the subcontractors?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think that is important because much as there has been an infraction at the process level, at the end of the day, this is a project that allows us to use materials that we would otherwise have really no use for.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the number of shoes that are discarded everyday amounts to a substantial number.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We intend to continue with this – whether it is at playgrounds or other sports facilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Zhulkarnain knows from our masterplan that there are plans to install sporting facilities in, as far as possible, every town that we have.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, many of these facilities will take advantage of and use these sustainable materials.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And all these can be put into the contract and the provisions for reporting.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, at the end of the day, I think it is also important to bear in mind that this is otherwise not a complicated contract nor a complicated arrangement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is really for an aggregator to come and go around the different bins to collect the shoes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it is really a question of taking the steps to ensure that there is proper segregation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we will certainly see the extent to which we can impart into these sub-contracts some other mechanisms that tighten the process without being overly burdensome, which then in turn increases the cost of collection.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Learning from this incident, how will the Ministry strengthen the process, such that credible partners will be selected for future recycling projects?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The point I will make is we do want partners to come forward with the assurance and confidence in the project that the shoes that are collected for a recycling project like this will, in fact, end up being the granules that we use for our sporting infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This is pertaining to the Reuters report, which I think, really, was addressing the prospect of greenwashing, or at least the concerns of greenwashing.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I do not really have any objection to the principles behind why this initiative was carried out by Sport Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think sustainability initiatives ought to be encouraged.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But my question pertains to whether Sport Singapore or MCCY made an assessment as to the conversion of sports shoes into rubber granules as being more green or more environmentally sustainable than the existing method which, as I understand also, uses this recycled tyres, for example.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, the question then is, does this initiative move the needle, or is it just a conversion of one recyclable material for another?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My understanding from people in the industry is a lot of these materials are then actually compressed together – tyres are used with rubber soles as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because each layer of the surface of a running track is made of different materials.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I would not get into the technicalities of it, of course, but I think the principle point remains with regard to ensuring that the method that SportSG adopts is actually more green and sustainable to ensure that programmes like this succeed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would not get into a debate over the efficacy of which material is best used for playgrounds and sports grounds and so on, but I will ensure that the point that you have raised is fed back to the relevant engineers so that they will study this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I will put to Mr Singh this – at the very least, this method does use the shoes as a further source of materials, when the shoes would otherwise be disposed of.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, if nothing else, the grinding facility provides an additional avenue for waste material.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I have said earlier in my answer, the number of shoes that are discarded, provides an avenue for these shoes to be reused in public infrastructure facilities.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The first is on the description of lax sorting at the downstream contractor Yok Impex.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Looking at the Reuters article of 25 February 2023, I may stand corrected, but there is a phrase that says, "none of the 11 pairs of shoes donated by Reuters were turned into exercise paths or kids' parks in Singapore”.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In view of this, what is the Ministry's assessment of how lax the sorting was, given that, none of 11 shoes donated by Reuters actually went to the intended purpose?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The second question is, do the authorities' investigations plan to look into whether any sub-contractor or their employee received inappropriate direct or secondary gains or even inappropriate gratification in conjunction with the redirection of these shoes that were meant to be recycled?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Tan, did any of the shoes belong to your Clementi residents?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I should declare, Mr Speaker, that I do have Clementi residents who have donated shoes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As to Dr Tan's first point, the way in which the system was working previously, was for Yok Impex, the sub-contractor, to collect from designated areas around Singapore and all of their collections would then be brought back to their facility for the sorting purposes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I cannot tell you nor can I glean from the Reuters' report where the shoes were deposited; whether they are all done at the same place or divided up into 11 different locations or otherwise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, I would not want to speculate as to why that is the case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the measures that Alba has taken in relation to Yok Impex would, in relation to the findings that we know so far, be sufficient to address the problem.
